claims.text: multi-shop-requirements.md is a draft by the product owner and the team, circulated for feedback before the architecture is chosen (ADR 0012); lines 3-5 say every number in it is the team's assumption, marked where it appears, not a measurement.

CH-1 to CH-4 (lines 23-30): a shop's users see and change only its own data; a new shop opens with no deploy, release or migration; one shop's busy day does not slow others' product reads and order placing; per-shop name, brand, email, changed without deploy.

Driver table (lines 32-42): isolation not needed -> required; opening shops never -> a few a week, no deploy; config shared -> per shop; a few large shops hold most orders, one up to 10% on its promotion day; orders/shop/day avg 50, max 5,000; one team -> three to four.

The table's last row and the section 'Không đổi' (lines 47-52) keep refunds (YC-1 to YC-10 of refund-requirements.md), order emails and order status rules unchanged inside each shop; what changes is that every row of data must know its shop.
Lines 44-45: total orders and product reads grow with the number of shops, but estimating load and capacity is separate work, not done in the requirements document.
The first open question (line 64) asks whether any contract demands a separate copy of the system for one shop, answered by the product owner with sales, before the architecture is chosen.

Drivers that change in kind: isolation of data (CH-1) and load (CH-3: one shop had no neighbor to slow), opening and configuring shops, and teams (someone must decide where teams meet). Busiest-shop and orders-per-shop figures only grow; sizing is separate.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 4; misconception 1; driver table lines 34-41; design.l4.conways-law

claims.text: When a driver stays the same inside each shop (refunds, emails, order rules), the parts built for it can keep their shape; the stable drivers matter to the architecture choice as much as the changed ones, because they say what must not be broken.
No changed driver names a service split: isolation must hold inside every service however the system is cut; the team row reopens where teams meet, which is not a rebuild.

Trade-offs: reading the change as a speed problem misses isolation, shop opening, settings and teams; reading it as a full rewrite redoes working parts no requirement asks to change; reading driver by driver costs a table to keep true and open questions, with assumed numbers.

Choices: answer the 'own copy' open question in the requirements before choosing; size volume in separate work when numbers are needed, since sizing cannot answer drivers that change in kind (CH-1, CH-2); a per-shop refund rule changes a driver the draft lists as stable.
